exposure: location of health facility (urban vs peri-urban)
cohort: A total of 500 pregnant women, comprising 270 urban and 230 peri-urban dwellers, attending selected health facilities in Ghana.
finding: Women attending urban health facilities were more likely to be hypertensive, have chronic hypertension with superimposed pre-eclampsia, have good quality ANC, deliver full term, and have excellent knowledge on HDPs compared to those in peri-urban facilities.
mod_finding: The method of delivery did not statistically vary between women attending peri-urban and urban health facilities.
cross-section timing: During pregnancy and at the time of birth, as assessed by outcomes related to HDPs and delivery term.
